name: Body Dao
summary: Preservation through form: the body is the foundation of all cultivation and a perfect form endures beyond worlds. It exists because form is the only reading legible from the three law groups a three-slot world can afford, which is why its authored home tier is mortal - and because mortal worlds license no humanoid, its own practitioners are visitors there.

attributes.philosophy: Preservation through form. The body is the foundation of all cultivation; a perfect form endures beyond worlds.
attributes.reads_spatial_law_as: a container that holds - the world is what the perfect form endures inside
attributes.practitioners_native_to_home_tier: none - mortal_world licenses plant and beast only, so Body Dao's home tier cannot produce a Body Dao practitioner

name: Dao Migration
summary: A Dao is native to one tier and imported into the rest, so no tier ever holds its own practitioners: mortal worlds license no humanoid, which means Body Dao's own people are not native to Body Dao's own tier. It exists to make the authored home_tier ladder a migration story rather than three unrelated labels.

attributes.the_ladder: body is native to the tier with no humanoids, qi to the first tier with humanoids, mind to the last - the authored home_tier values are the tier ladder read backwards
attributes.body_dao_case: mortal_world licenses plant and beast only and every authored humanoid begins at spirit_world, so Body Dao's home tier cannot produce a humanoid practitioner at all
attributes.what_actually_migrates: the reading, not the population - a Dao arrives in a tier as a practice that tier's own law set cannot quite support
attributes.cost: a law scar on return; the practitioner's home imprint is gone and the outline remains
attributes.product: form_only_dao, a heresy born because migrating Body Dao arrived where qi was already spent
attributes.immortal_tier_gap: immortal_world is the only tier no Dao is native to, which makes it the tier everything passes through

name: Dao Slot Budget
summary: Each Dao is legible from a three-group subset, and home_tier is the lowest tier whose slot budget can hold that subset - which is why body=mortal at three slots, qi=spirit at six, and mind=transcendent, where spatial must be read high enough for a self to outgrow its body. It exists to derive the authored home_tier values rather than describe them.

attributes.rule: home_tier is the lowest tier whose law_slots can hold the three-group subset the Dao reads, at working values
attributes.body_dao_read: physical + life + spatial = 3 slots; mortal_world offers exactly 3 and offers nothing spare, so it is native there and has no room to become anything else
attributes.qi_dao_read: qi + temporal + physical = 3 slots, but qi and temporal only reach working values where the budget can also carry element, because qi without an element has no type; spirit_world at 6 slots is the first tier that can
attributes.mind_dao_read: spatial + temporal + qi = 3 slots, but spatial must be read at the high end of its 0.1-10 range because the practice is the self leaving a body, and only a 10000-100000 unit world can hold a container that big
attributes.authored_values_matched: body_dao=mortal_world, qi_dao=spirit_world, mind_dao=transcendent_world, all three reproduced from the rule rather than fitted to it
attributes.stance_explained: body and qi share physical_law so they are neutral; qi and mind share qi_law and temporal_law so they are allied; body and mind share spatial_law and read it oppositely - as a container that holds against an exit the self leaves by - so they are hostile
attributes.immortal_world_holds_no_home: the immortal tier has 10 slots and hosts no Dao's home, because mind_dao's subset already works there while body_dao's and qi_dao's read better lower down

name: Dao Variable
summary: A Dao is not a school of thought but a locally dominant reading of a world law set: where one group is imprinted strongly enough to organise daily life, a philosophy crystallises around the way that group behaves. It exists so Dao can move with geography, and so the same principle is taught differently above and below a tier line.

attributes.what_a_dao_is: the interpretation of an imprinted law group that a world's inhabitants actually live by
attributes.why_it_varies: a group read at the floor of its range gives a different practice from the same group read high, so a Dao differs between a strained world and a common one
attributes.not_a_school: no founder, no curriculum and no admission; a Dao is what a world is shaped into, which is why the three factions hold territory instead of running academies
attributes.the_test: if a world rewrote its law set, the Dao would change without anyone deciding to change it
attributes.authored_note: the three Dao factions carry dao_alignment and home_tier and are otherwise identical in shape, which is what a world-variable looks like as data

name: Elemental Deficiency
summary: In a mortal-tier world nothing carries an element because elemental_law was never written: seasons drift unanchored, ore has no affinity, and an elemental is a life form no law licenses. It exists to answer why the tier a mortal actually lives in has weather but no elemental anything at all.

attributes.why_unwritten: the three mortal slots are pinned by what the tier's only content requires - physical for iron_ore, life for herb_common, qi for a beast's 5-50 combat power; nothing in that list needs an element
attributes.consequence_seasons: elemental_law governs seasonal cycles, and unwritten it leaves the year as weather rather than law, so it recurs without anything holding it to a cycle
attributes.consequence_ore: iron_ore carries no elemental affinity, so no elemental treasure can form here and none can be forged toward one from here
attributes.consequence_life_form: storm_elemental is authored native to immortal_world and transcendent_world only - nothing is licensing an elemental below that
attributes.consequence_damage: elemental damage has nothing to act on; there is no elemental share in a substance to strike
attributes.not_a_weakening: elemental_law is available in the mortal tier because its authored tier_ids list all four tiers; it is simply unspent, which is a different failure from being forbidden
attributes.cost_to_a_practitioner: an elemental technique is learnable anywhere and usable nowhere in this tier - the realm is reachable and the effect is not

name: Elemental Emergence
summary: An elemental is the first life form needing three law groups written into one body at once, so it appears exactly where a layer's share of the budget can gather them: the immortal tier's ten slots, and not before. It exists to move elemental life from a setting detail to an arithmetic consequence of concentration.

attributes.why_not_spirit: a six-slot spirit-tier world holds all three groups but must spread six imprints over 100-1000 units, so no single body gathers them; ten slots over a layered immortal world is the first budget that can
attributes.authored_evidence: storm_elemental lists immortal_world and transcendent_world only, with combat_power_min 100.0 - the tier where it appears is also the tier where the budget jumps
attributes.consequence: elementals are the first inhabitants a law budget can create on its own, which is why immortal_court staffs itself with humanoid and elemental rather than hiring
attributes.why_danger_8: the same law concentration that makes an elemental possible in immortal_court is what makes anything formed there violently stable

name: Elemental Law
summary: Governs dominant elements, elemental balance, and seasonal cycles.

name: Form-Only Dao
summary: What migrating Body Dao becomes where qi is already spent: it wins with physical_law alone, and it is recorded as a heresy rather than a school because nothing in a three-slot world can test the claim. It exists because an unwritten law does not merely restrict practice - it invents one.

attributes.descends_from: Body Dao's form-permanence claim with the qi component removed
attributes.why_it_appears: a mortal-tier world spends its qi slot at the floor of the range, so a practitioner who cannot draw qi anyway is pushed to the same conclusion independently, which makes the heresy reproducible rather than eccentric
attributes.the_claim: form persists without charge - refine until nothing is left to be destroyed, and treat every expenditure of qi as an avoidable loss
attributes.why_disputed: no court at a realm above the mortal band has ever tested it against a realm-19 body, so nothing has falsified it; it is unrefuted rather than proven
attributes.what_would_refute_it: one practitioner reaching a realm-19 breakthrough on form alone, or one failing while holding the same form in a world where qi was available
attributes.ceiling: a strained qi_law never carries the practice high, so the ceiling is the world's floor rather than the practitioner's skill

name: Immortal-Tier Law Availability
summary: Ten slots cannot fit in one layer's six, so the surplus forces a second layer with its own law list - the first tier where a world is layered rather than single. It exists because the slot budget is what makes an elemental body possible here: three groups finally gathered in one place.

attributes.layer_split: at least two; ten imprints over six groups leaves four to duplicate, and a duplicate only has somewhere to sit if a second layer exists
attributes.second_layer_forced: a second layer at this tier is arithmetic, not decoration
attributes.anchor_site: geography.immortal_court - immortal_essence and star_metal, humanoid and elemental inhabitants, danger_level 8
attributes.clock_drift: temporal_law readable to 50x, so a mortal lifespan inside an immortal world is a rounding error and upkeep rather than lifespan is what kills

name: Immortal World
summary: The third tier: realms 19-27, ten law slots - more imprints than there are laws, so a second layer with its own law list is forced by arithmetic. It exists because ten is the first budget that can gather three law groups into one body, which is the tier where elemental life becomes possible.

attributes.second_layer_forced: ten imprints over six groups leaves four duplicates, and a duplicate needs somewhere to sit
attributes.elemental_tier: the first tier whose budget can gather elemental, physical and qi into one body, and the tier storm_elemental first appears in

name: Law Imprint
summary: An imprint is one law group written into one layer at one authored value - presence as a magnitude rather than a yes or no. It exists because every authored law carries value_min and value_max, so a law is a dial, and a slot spends one setting of that dial rather than the whole law.

attributes.what_it_is: one law group, one layer, one value inside that group's authored range
attributes.authored_ranges: physical 0.1-10.0, spatial 0.1-10.0, qi 0.1-100.0, temporal 0.1-100.0, elemental 0.0-1.0, life 0.0-1.0
attributes.reads_as: common when high in range, strained at the floor, unwritten when no imprint exists at all, or torn when driven outside value_max or below value_min
attributes.failure_signature: an imprint pushed past value_max or below value_min stops holding and leaves its layer exposed; that is the only way a rift forms
attributes.one_slot_spends: one setting of one dial, not the whole law

name: Law Scar
summary: A scar is the place a law used to be written and no longer is, left by a world that gave up an imprint to pay upkeep or to grow past it. It exists because the tier ladder is not additive: a body trained in a set that no longer holds meets a hole shaped like the thing it lost.

attributes.what_it_is: the negative space of a withdrawn imprint, still inside a layer that used to hold it
attributes.how_it_forms: an imprint is dropped to free a slot or to cut upkeep, and the layer keeps the outline
attributes.why_the_ladder_is_not_additive: ascending adds imprints and descending removes them; the removal leaves a scar, so a returning body meets the difference as an injury rather than as a weaker ability
attributes.reads_as: a place where an authored technique produces nothing at all rather than a reduced number - an unwritten law's failure mode at full strength
attributes.who_leaves_them: worlds that merged, and worlds that paid a tier's upkeep by surrendering the imprint the next tier would have required
attributes.runtime_analogue: WorldState.stability losing severity * 0.1 per conflict; a scar is stability lost without a fight

name: Unwritten Law
summary: An unimprinted group is not weak, it is absent, and absence has exactly three signatures: no process runs on it, no substance carries it, and no life form is licensed by it. It exists as the rule that turns unspent slots into a real absence, which is the whole cost side of a small law budget.

attributes.definition: a law group no layer of this world holds an imprint of
attributes.three_signatures: no process - nothing in the world changes because of it; no substance - no material in the world carries it; no life form - nothing alive is built out of it
attributes.why_not_merely_weak: a strained law is present at the floor of its range and can be pushed; an unwritten law cannot be pushed because there is no dial to push
attributes.the_cost_side_of: the slots a tier does not spend
attributes.recoverable: only by writing the imprint, which costs a slot and then costs upkeep every period after
attributes.failure_mode: where a law is unwritten a technique fails at full strength - not reduced, absent

name: Life Law
summary: Governs allowed life forms, evolution speed, and intelligence ceiling.

name: Mind Dao
summary: Transcendence through spirit: the mind is the seed of the Dao and refining the self touches the infinite. It exists because the self leaving a body needs spatial_law read high - a self larger than its container - and only a 10000-100000 unit world at fifteen slots makes that arithmetic work, which is why its home tier is the top one.

attributes.philosophy: Transcendence through spirit. The mind is the seed of the Dao; to refine the self is to touch the infinite.
attributes.reads_spatial_law_as: an exit - refining the self touches the infinite, so the container is what is left behind
attributes.why_top_tier: spatial_law must be read at the high end of its 0.1-10 range and only the top tier's size and slot budget hold a self that outgrows its container

name: Mortal-Tier Law Availability
summary: A mortal-tier world spends all three slots on the three groups its only content needs - physical for ore, life for herbs, qi for a beast's strength - so elemental, spatial and temporal are never written. It exists to explain why nothing elemental, nothing born of a season and no traveller can exist in the tier a mortal actually lives in.

attributes.reads_near_floor: qi_law sits at the bottom of its 0.1-100 range - enough that a seed germinates, a body draws breath and an ironhide bear reaches combat power 5, not enough for a dantian to fill
attributes.spatial_by_default: spatial_law is the unspent group that would have mattered most: unwritten, the size band 10-100 units is a ceiling rather than a range, which is why a mortal world cannot grow into a spirit world
attributes.anchor_site: geography.mortal_plains - iron_ore and herb_common, beast inhabitants only
attributes.resident_yield: nothing elemental can be alive to hold an elemental resource, so the tier yields none
attributes.humanoids: not licensed; every authored humanoid inhabitant begins at spirit_world, so the tier's own practitioners are visitors

name: Mortal World
summary: The lowest tier: realms 1-9, three law slots, plant and beast life only, worlds 10-100 units across. It exists as the rung everything starts on, and its limit is arithmetic rather than moral - a world holding three of six law groups cannot practise what the other three permit, so the first realm ladder is also the shortest.

attributes.what_it_cannot: no humanoid, no elemental, no anchored season, no growth past 100 units, and no practitioner of Body Dao - which is its own home tier's Dao

name: Physical Law
summary: Governs gravity, energy density, and material hardness.

name: Qi Dao
summary: Creation through energy: the universe is qi in motion and to shape qi is to shape reality. It exists because energy is the reading that needs a tier able to carry qi, temporal and element at working values together, which the authored data puts at spirit - the first tier where anything humanoid lives to practise it.

attributes.philosophy: Creation through energy. The universe is qi in motion; to shape qi is to shape reality.
attributes.why_home_is_spirit: qi and temporal reach working values only where the budget can also carry element, because qi without an element has no type; spirit_world at six slots is the first tier that can, and the first tier with a humanoid population
attributes.only_dao_with_a_native_population: spirit_world licenses humanoids, so this is the only Dao that is home, native and staffed by its own kind at once

name: Qi Law
summary: Governs qi density, qi type, and qi tide cycles.

name: Qi Tide
summary: A tide is an authored law value moving through its range on a cycle, which is why breakthroughs are scheduled to them: a tide is the only cheap way a strained law ever reads as a common one. It exists because every law is authored as a range, and a range that never moved would make the ceiling of a strained law permanent.

attributes.what_it_is: the periodic movement of a law's value inside its authored range, authored into qi_law's own description as qi tide cycles
attributes.why_it_must_exist: all six laws are authored with value_min and value_max; a value that never moved would make the range decorative and the ceiling of a strained law permanent
attributes.amplitude_rule: a tide cannot raise a law above value_max; a surge that reaches the end of the range is out of range, and an out-of-range imprint tears
attributes.what_it_is_for: timing - a strained law rides up on a tide, so a breakthrough scheduled to a crest can be attempted at a strength the world cannot otherwise produce
attributes.mortal_case: a mortal-tier tide on a 0.1 qi_law is too thin to cultivate on and too real to ignore; it is the whole of a mortal's life as one long trough with brief crests
attributes.reads_also_as: season, weather, and the unevenness in resource yield that every geography downstream has to explain

name: Realm Band
summary: A realm is a band of a law value, not a rank of a person: the ladder's four bands are contiguous ranges of what a body can survive the world's law set doing to it. It exists so a mortal world's ceiling at realm 9 reads as a property of its three imprints rather than as a rule about how hard someone tried.

attributes.what_a_realm_is: a range of tolerated law pressure; above it the body stops being a stable container
attributes.why_a_band_ends_where_it_does: a tier's band ends where its imprints run out, not where its inhabitants run out - three imprints carry a body to 9 and no further
attributes.not_a_merit_ranking: the same realm number in a smaller world describes a body held closer to its tolerance, so a spirit-tier realm 10 is not a promotion over a mortal-tier one - it is a different tier's band
attributes.what_breaks_past_the_band: the body, never the technique; the meridian network fails first because it is the most numerous and least redundant, and the sea fails last because it is the only reservoir
attributes.tide_interaction: a tide carries the band's pressure up briefly, so a realm can be touched at the top of a tide and not held at the bottom of one
attributes.ceiling_is_not_content: the ladder stops at 30 because thirty realms are authored; that is a content decision, not a cosmological argument that a band past 30 could not exist

name: Rift
summary: A rift is an imprint that has failed - a law value pushed past value_max or below value_min, where the group no longer holds - and it is the only event that makes two worlds adjacent. It exists to give travel a cause inside the authored ranges and to say what closes one: the value returning in range.

attributes.cause: an imprint driven outside its authored range - qi past 100, temporal past 100, spatial past 10 - so the group stops holding and the layer's outline is left exposed
attributes.the_sole_mechanism: a rift is the only way one world becomes reachable from another; nothing else in the setting brings two worlds adjacent
attributes.what_opens_a_path: the two sides must agree on at least one group at one value; where they do, a body can cross, and where they agree on nothing a tear opens onto a wall
attributes.what_closes_it: the value coming back inside the range, so rifts close on the same cycle tides run on and a permanent passage is always a claim about a law value rather than a permanent hole
attributes.where_it_happens_first: the highest-budget worlds, because they are the only ones with enough imprints gathered close enough to push one of them off the end; a three-slot mortal world has nothing left to overpress
attributes.cost_to_cross: the traveller's own imprint set is at risk - arriving into a different set meets an unwritten group, and returning meets the law scar left by the departure

name: Slot Budget
summary: A slot is one law written at one value into one layer, so law_slots counts imprints and not distinct laws - which is why a fifteen-slot transcendent world is not a world holding fifteen laws. It exists because six groups cannot fill 3/6/10/15, and layers are what make the larger budgets mean anything.

attributes.what_one_slot_is: one law group at one authored value, held by one layer, since an authored WorldLayerState carries its own law list and its own size ratio
attributes.why_more_slots_than_laws: a group may be imprinted at more than one value in different layers of the same world; the budget counts imprints, so it can exceed six
attributes.every_law_is_a_dial: value_min and value_max are authored on all six laws, so presence is a magnitude rather than a yes, and a slot spends one setting of a dial
attributes.not_enforced_in_runtime: WorldState.add_law appends with no cap and WorldApi.add_law never reads law_slots; WorldApi also carries its own micro/small/great tier vocabulary with no WorldTierDef data and computes new_law_slots as (idx+2)*3 for 3/6/9, matching the authored mortal and spirit budgets and diverging from immortal 10 and transcendent 15

name: Spatial Law
summary: Governs world size, dimensions, and spatial stability.

name: Spirit-Tier Law Availability
summary: Six slots is the first budget that can hold all six groups, so a spirit-tier world is the first where nothing is merely missing - but it still cannot gather three groups into one body, which is why elementals wait. It exists to mark the exact tier where law stops being the constraint and room inside a layer becomes it.

attributes.concentrated_in_one_layer: not affordable; six imprints must cover 100-1000 units, so no single body gathers three groups in one place
attributes.why_elementals_wait: an elemental body is three groups in one shell, and holding all three is not the same as gathering them
attributes.anchor_site: geography.spirit_peaks - spirit_stone and jade_ore, beast and humanoid inhabitants
attributes.humanoids: first licensed here, which is why qi_dao - the only Dao whose home tier this is - is also the first Dao with a native population
attributes.time_flood: temporal_law readable to 10x makes spirit-tier lives feel brief and its breakthroughs quick, and is the first tier where a person's own lifespan is a discount against the world's clock

name: Spirit World
summary: The second tier: realms 10-18, six law slots - the first budget that can hold all six law groups - plant, beast and humanoid life, worlds 100-1000 units. It exists as the tier where law stops being the constraint and room inside a layer becomes it, which is why the first humanoids and the first Dao both land here.

attributes.first_full_law_set: six slots is the first budget equal to the six authored groups, so this is the first tier where nothing is merely unspent
attributes.first_humanoid_tier: humanoids are licensed here and nowhere below, which makes this the only tier that is a Dao's home, native and staffed at once

name: Strained Law
summary: A strained law is imprinted at the floor of its authored range: it runs, and nothing can be done to it. It exists because it is what fills the gap a small budget leaves - a mortal world's qi is not missing, it is present at 0.1, and that is the entire difference between a world and a place qi has left.

attributes.definition: a law imprinted at or near value_min, inside its authored range
attributes.signature: works, and resists - every attempt to push it up spends qi and returns the same reading
attributes.canonical_case: qi_law at 0.1 in a mortal-tier world: enough that a seed germinates, a beast reaches 5-50 combat power and a body draws breath, not enough for a dantian to fill
attributes.contrast: an unwritten law has no dial; a strained law has a dial wired to the floor
attributes.why_it_exists: so a three-slot world is limited rather than empty, and so a breakthrough's difficulty is a property of the world's setting rather than of the student
attributes.the_escape: a tide carries it above the floor for a while, which is the only cheap way out and the reason breakthroughs are timed rather than merely attempted

name: Temporal Law
summary: Governs time flow rate and temporal stability within the world.

name: Three-Dao Split
summary: A single unified Dao would need all six groups legible at once, which is a fifteen-slot budget, so three is not a tradition's taste: it is the largest number of coherent readings a six-slot spirit-tier world can hold. It exists to explain why the setting has three Dao and not one.

attributes.why_not_one: a unified Dao must read all six groups together at once, which needs a budget no tier below transcendent_world carries
attributes.why_three: three is the largest number of coherent readings a six-slot spirit-tier world can hold, since each needs its own three-group subset and the subsets must not compete for the same slots
attributes.why_not_four: a fourth Dao would need a fifth group read on its own, and no fifth group exists - the six WorldLawDef resources are the entire vocabulary, so self-sufficient readings are bounded by the vocabulary and not by history
attributes.two_would_be_wrong: two readings would leave a spirit-tier world's six slots with room to spare, and a reading with room to spare is a preference rather than a reading
attributes.three_subsets: body reads physical + life + spatial; qi reads qi + temporal + physical; mind reads spatial + temporal + qi
attributes.the_asymmetry: body and qi overlap on exactly one group and are neutral; qi and mind overlap on two and are allied; body and mind overlap on one and use it oppositely, which is why they are hostile

name: Transcendent-Tier Law Availability
summary: Fifteen slots need three layers, which is why a transcendent world is built rather than grown: no single will holds fifteen imprints spread over three law lists. It exists as the ceiling the setting needs - the only budget large enough for a unified Dao, and the only tier whose shortage is will rather than law.

attributes.creation_not_growth: reaching this budget is an act of will rather than accumulation; the runtime gates world merging at 1.5x the target will_strength for the same reason
attributes.three_layers: fifteen imprints over six groups needs three law lists, so a world this size is layered or it is incoherent
attributes.anchor_site: geography.transcendent_realm - dao_fragment and void_crystal, humanoid and elemental inhabitants, danger_level 10
attributes.what_is_scarce: not law - all six groups are present at high values. What is scarce is a will strong enough to hold fifteen at once, which is why a world this size must be fed or merged and never merely left alone

name: Transcendent World
summary: The top tier: realms 28-30, fifteen law slots, worlds 10000-100000 units, upkeep 5-20. It exists as a ceiling the setting needs rather than a reward for arriving: fifteen imprints over three layers take a will to hold, so a world this size is built or merged, never grown.

attributes.creation_not_growth: fifteen imprints spread over three layers exceed what one will holds, so a world at this tier is built by a breakthrough or assembled by merging, and merging is gated on 1.5x the target will_strength
attributes.the_only_unified_dao_budget: the only tier whose budget can hold all six groups at working values in one layer, which is what makes a single unified Dao arithmetic rather than heresy here

name: Universe
summary: A universe is the closed budget of six law groups that exists once and whole; every world inside it holds a subset, never a seventh. It exists as a countable thing because a ceiling must be scarce against something, and the authored tiers need the six laws to be a fixed supply that tiers compete over rather than an open list.

attributes.what_it_is: the complete six-group law budget plus the worlds competing to imprint subsets of it
attributes.what_it_is_not: not a place - it has no size, no time flow and no life forms, so none of the four tier definitions apply to it
attributes.shares_one_law_set: yes; a group is identical everywhere inside a universe, and only whether it is imprinted, and at what value, differs between worlds
attributes.drifts: no; a universe cannot acquire or lose a group, only re-imprint one at another value
attributes.why_it_exists: so the six authored laws are a finite supply that law_slots compete against, instead of an open list every tier could extend
attributes.the_world_distinction: a world is a single budget holder; a universe is the budget itself

name: World Boundary
summary: A world boundary is not a wall between neighbours but the edge of a law budget: crossing it means arriving where a group you relied on is unwritten. It exists to make travel rare for a structural reason rather than a logistical one, because a path is opened by two worlds agreeing on one group and by nothing else.

attributes.what_it_is: the surface where one world's imprint list stops and another's begins
attributes.why_travel_is_rare: a body is built to the imprint set it grew in, and arriving where a required group is unwritten is an injury rather than a handicap - an unwritten group's failure mode is absent, not reduced
attributes.what_a_traveller_carries: not power but tolerance; a realm band is a band of one world's law values, so it is valid across a boundary only over the overlap
attributes.high_realm_is_a_liability: the higher a body is tuned, the more finely it reads one world and the more brittle it is in another, so a realm is a passport and a fragility at once
attributes.why_not_a_wall: two sides are not adjacent and cannot be walked to; a boundary is a disagreement, not a barrier with a door
attributes.what_makes_a_path: an overlap - one group imprinted at the same value in both worlds - which is the whole mechanism, and why power opens nothing
attributes.default_state: closed; a world holding itself together is at equilibrium and has no reason to tear, so isolation is the normal condition of a world

name: World Layer
summary: A layer is one region of a world - surface, under, heaven, void - carrying its own law list and its own share of the volume. It exists because a world's law_slots exceed the number of laws from the immortal tier up, so the surplus has to go somewhere, and layers are the only place it can go.

attributes.what_it_is: a region of a world with its own law list and its own size ratio, authored as WorldLayerState(layer_id, name, size_ratio, laws)
attributes.why_it_exists: so law_slots can exceed six without duplicating a group inside one layer
attributes.surface_only_world: a mortal-tier world at three slots has one layer, so its surface law list is its entire law set
attributes.minimum_by_tier: one layer up to spirit_world, two at immortal_world where ten imprints need somewhere to sit, three at transcendent_world where fifteen do
attributes.difference_from_a_region: a geography region is a place inside a layer; a layer is a place with its own laws
